The original wrote a local temp archive, uploaded it, then ran a staged extract with backup and rollback; this stream packs tar.gz into the remote tar over the same connection's exec channel, extracts into a sibling .netcatty-extract-* directory, and promotes each target by rename. Every extracted entry is read back before promotion: a directory must be a directory and a file's size must equal the plan (ADR-0012). Any preflight refusal, unsafe name, symlink, special file, move, conflict, resume row, extraction failure, short extraction, or cancellation never publishes partial data; a failed extraction is removed and the ordinary per-file copy runs instead. The packer reads one byte past each planned size so a source that grew is refused instead of publishing a prefix. An exec transport that cannot half-close is refused before any byte is written rather than risking a killed tar. |

destination-only folder content. An apply-to-all answer is scoped to one batch and conflict type and covers the remaining conflicts without a second prompt; without it only the row that asked is answered. The prompt's count names only the same-type conflicts that will actually follow, and the choice is offered only when at least one exists, so a new sibling is not counted as a conflict. Duplicate names and top-level destination paths, including whole directory subtrees, are reserved at enqueue or plan time, so two concurrent Transfers cannot stage into one path; a duplicate reserves only the name it chose, and a paused row keeps that name, as does a retried row reclaiming its destination. A Transfer refused because another one owns the destination reports the reserved message rather than the generic operation failure. A merge compares size and whole-second mtime and leaves an unchanged destination untouched, counting it as skipped. A file that meets a destination directory during a merge fails as a type mismatch instead of deleting the directory's subtree. |
